questions.question: How do you detect and reduce overfitting in a machine learning model?
key_points: Gap between training and validation performance
Uses a held-out set or cross-validation
Regularization such as L1, L2 or dropout
More or augmented data, simpler model, early stopping

questions.question: You are building a fraud detection model where only 1% of transactions are fraud. How would you evaluate it?
key_points: Accuracy is misleading on imbalanced data
Precision, recall, F1 and the precision-recall curve
Chooses the decision threshold by the business cost of errors
Stratified splits; handles imbalance with class weights or resampling

questions.question: Explain how the attention mechanism in a transformer works and why it replaced recurrent networks for most language tasks.
key_points: Queries, keys and values; weights from scaled dot products and softmax
Each token can attend to every other token directly
Processes the sequence in parallel, unlike RNNs
Handles long-range dependencies better
Positional encodings supply word order

questions.question: How would you design a retrieval-augmented generation system to answer questions over a company's internal documents?
key_points: Chunks documents and creates embeddings
Stores them in a vector database or search index
Retrieves relevant chunks, optionally hybrid search and reranking
Puts retrieved context in the prompt and cites sources
Evaluates retrieval quality and answer faithfulness

questions.question: How do you evaluate the quality of an LLM-based application before and after it goes to production?
key_points: Builds a test set of representative inputs with expected outputs
Uses automatic metrics, LLM-as-judge and human review
Checks for hallucination, safety and format errors
Monitors in production with logging and user feedback
Runs regression tests when prompts or models change

questions.question: Walk me through how you would take a trained model to production and serve it reliably.
key_points: Packages the model with versioned artifacts and dependencies
Serves it behind an API, batch job or streaming pipeline
Containers and CI/CD for repeatable releases
Considers latency, throughput, scaling and cost
Safe rollout such as canary, shadow or A/B testing

questions.question: After deployment, a model's performance slowly degrades. How would you find out why and fix it?
key_points: Monitors input data and prediction distributions
Distinguishes data drift from concept drift
Checks for upstream data pipeline or feature bugs
Retrains on fresh data and compares against the current model
Sets alerts and a retraining process

questions.question: When would you fine-tune a model instead of using prompt engineering or retrieval, and what are the trade-offs?
key_points: Prompting and retrieval are cheaper and faster to change
Retrieval suits knowledge that changes or must be cited
Fine-tuning suits consistent style, format or a narrow task
Fine-tuning needs quality labelled data and costs more to maintain
Mentions parameter-efficient methods such as LoRA

questions.question: What is data leakage, and how have you prevented it in your projects?
key_points: Information from outside the training data or from the future leaks into features
Leads to good offline scores but poor real-world performance
Splits data before preprocessing and fits transforms on training data only
Uses time-based splits for time series

questions.question: Your model is accurate but too slow and expensive to serve. What options would you consider?
key_points: Smaller model or knowledge distillation
Quantization or pruning
Batching and caching
Hardware choices such as GPU or optimized runtimes
Measures the accuracy cost of each change
